$comment: T16 (D4 / OV2 correction #10) — connection-budget ratchet. scripts/check-connection-budget.ts flags a `new ...Pool(` call site not guarded by the codebase's lazy-singleton memoization pattern nearby — i.e. a pool that looks like it gets rebuilt on every call. Every entry below is a REAL finding from the T16 audit, not a false positive: each one is safe TODAY only because it happens to run exactly once per process (module-top-level, or a class instantiated exactly once via a memoized factory elsewhere in its file) rather than because it's memoized the way the script checks for. They are deliberately left on this list rather than migrated in the same pass that added the check — see docs/ops/render-database-url.md's audit table for the full reasoning and priority order. An addition here must be reviewed and must explain, in the entry's own comment, why the flagged call site is actually safe; do not add an entry just to silence the check.

_reasoning.src/api/blog-routes.ts:22: Module-top-level `const pool = new pg.Pool(...)` — constructed exactly once, when the module is first imported (Node's module cache). No `max` set (pg default: 10). Follow-up: migrate to getSharedPool() — flagged as a priority item in the T16 audit because three near-identical top-level pools (this one, funnel-routes, notification-routes) plus server.ts's ssrPool sum to 40 default-sized connections that exist purely because each file wrote its own copy instead of sharing one.
_reasoning.src/api/funnel-routes.ts:20: Same pattern and same follow-up as blog-routes.ts:22.
_reasoning.src/api/notification-routes.ts:21: Same pattern and same follow-up as blog-routes.ts:22.
_reasoning.src/server.ts:135: `ssrPool`, module-top-level, constructed once at import for server-rendered page routes. Same pattern as the three api/*-routes.ts pools above; same follow-up. (Line shifted 131→132 when the C1/C2 buyer-demo-prep change added one import line above it, then 132→133 when W3.2 added the attempt-skip-drill route import, then 133→134 when W1.3 added the admin review-queue route import, then 134→135 when the live-QA content-spec pass added the admin-content-spec-routes import — same call site every time, not a new one.)
_reasoning.src/server.ts:958: `migratePool`, built once inside main() at boot to run auto-migrate + the static PYQ seed (and now also the Linear Algebra practice-item seed, src/db/seed-la-practice-items.ts — same migratePool instance, no new Pool construction), then never referenced again (and never `.end()`-ed) for the rest of the process's life. Small (`max: 2`) and boot-only, so low severity, but it is a real leaked handle — follow-up: either close it after the boot sequence finishes, or run boot-time migration/seed through getSharedPool() instead. (Line shifted 945→946, then 946→950, then 950→954, then 954→958, for the same reason as ssrPool above — each pass added one import line and a three-to-four-line route-registration loop above this call site; the live-QA content-spec pass added the admin-content-spec-routes pair.)
_reasoning.src/sessions/session-store.ts:142: `PostgresStore`'s constructor. The class itself is a safe lazy singleton (`getSessionStore()` in the same file only calls `new PostgresStore()` once, behind an `if (!_store)` guard) — but that guard lives in a DIFFERENT function than the constructor, which is exactly the shape the heuristic can't see (see this script's header comment re: motivation-source-pg.ts, which had the identical shape before being migrated). No `max` set (pg default: 10), and this is genuinely one of the hottest paths in the app (every session read/write). Highest-priority follow-up on this list — migrating it is the natural next module after this pass's readiness/scoring/gbrain-student-model/quiz-xp-store set.
